title: The Receptionist by Adam Bock at Second Stage #thereceptionist #2stny...
transcript: It's often the most unassuming places where the shadiest work is done. In The Receptionist, it's business as usual at the office for Beverly until a man from “the central office” arrives looking for one of her office mates. Even during the first part of the play when everything's super mundane, things feel really off and you don't quite know why. This production smartly uses mood setting almost as foreshadowing, as you can tell that whatever this company does can't be good, before anything is explicitly mentioned about it. The play is sparing in its flow of information, but paced in a way that's consistently intriguing. It's definitely a comedy, but humorous in an uncomfortable or unsettling way that worked really well for me. I also enjoyed Katie Finneran and Mallori Johnson's performances and their hilarious prop work, especially one flirtatious moment that occurs involving a borrowed pen. Some folks may prefer a more definitive ending here, but I thought there was more than enough to draw your own conclusions. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer praises the mood-setting, pacing, humor, and performances with clear enthusiasm and no significant caveats beyond acknowledging some may want a more definitive ending, which he personally didn't mind.
